prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Overall vision
- Make the Liberal Democrats the strong opposition; no coalition with Conservatives or Corbyn’s Labour.
- Build an open, tolerant, united Britain; oppose a hard Brexit.

Europe/Brexit
- Second referendum on the final deal, with the option to remain.
- Press to stay in the single market/customs union; guarantee EU/UK citizens’ rights; protect Erasmus+, EHIC, roaming, and security cooperation (Europol/EAW).
- Safeguard environmental, social, consumer and workers’ rights; support science funding and City access.

NHS and social care
- Immediate 1p Income Tax rise (ringfenced) to raise £6bn for NHS/social care; plan a dedicated health and care tax; independent OBR-style budget monitor.
- Integrate health and social care; cap social care costs; support carers.
- Workforce: guarantee EU staff rights, end pay cap, restore nurse bursaries, national workforce plan.
- Mental health parity: waiting-time standards, crisis care, end out-of-area placements, perinatal and youth support.
- Prevention: restore public health funding; obesity strategy; smoking levy; PrEP on NHS; AMR action.

Education and skills
- Nearly £7bn extra: protect per-pupil funding; fair formula; protect Pupil Premium.
- Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium; boost quality.
- Oppose new grammar schools; return places planning to local authorities; allow Ofsted to inspect academy chains.
- Teachers: end 1% pay cap; funded CPD; reduce workload.
- Curriculum: slimmed national core incl PSHE/SRE (consent, LGBT+); protect arts; better careers/vocational routes.
- Pupil wellbeing: mental health support; free school meals for all primaries; breakfast clubs.
- Universities: reinstate maintenance grants; protect research/EU programmes; review finance.
- Lifelong learning: expand apprenticeships, adult learning accounts, basic skills by 2030.

Economy and jobs
- Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; borrow £100bn for infrastructure (300k homes/year, fibre-to-premises nationwide, transport, schools/hospitals, renewables); create Housing & Infrastructure Bank.
- Fair taxes: anti-avoidance, consider land value tax; reverse some Conservative tax cuts.
- SMEs/startups: expand British Business Bank; start-up allowance; business rates reform.
- Workers’ rights: genuine living wage, tackle zero-hours abuse, tribunal fees scrapped, gig-economy reforms.
- Regional growth: devolution with funding; local banking; procurement for local growth; wellbeing strategy.

Environment
- Five green laws (transport, zero carbon, nature, buildings, zero waste).
- Air quality plan: diesel scrappage; ban new diesel cars/small vans by 2025; expand ULEZ; EV infrastructure.
- Climate/energy: net zero by 2050; 60% renewables by 2030; support CCS; oppose fracking; accept nuclear with conditions; stay in Euratom.
- Homes: 4m insulation retrofits by 2022; zero-carbon new homes; expand community energy.
- Nature/farming: £2bn flood fund; Nature Act; tree planting; animal welfare; reform farm support toward public goods; high import standards; sustainable fisheries.
- Zero waste: 70% recycling by 2022; coffee cup charge; landfill/incineration reforms.

Families, housing, transport
- Childcare: expand free hours (from 9 months for working parents prioritised); extra month shared parental leave; day-one flexible work right.
- Fair welfare: uprate benefits; scrap two-child cap/“rape clause,” bedroom tax; raise LHA; reform disability assessments; winter fuel for non-higher-rate pensioners.
- Housing: 300k homes/year; 10 garden cities; lift council borrowing caps; curb land-banking; renters’ reforms (ban fees, cap deposits, longer tenancies, Help to Rent, Rent to Own); end rough sleeping via Housing First.
- Transport: rail electrification, HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2; fix failing franchises; 16–21 Bus Discount Card; devolve and improve buses; cycling/walking.

Rights, justice, immigration
- Defend HRA/ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; Leveson II; stronger FOI.
- Equalities: pay/transparency duties; mixed-sex civil partnerships; trans rights; decriminalise sex work; free period products in schools.
- Policing/justice: +£300m for community policing; body cams; restorative justice; presumption against short sentences; women’s justice board.
- Drugs: end prison for possession; legal, regulated cannabis market.
- Immigration/asylum: efficient, fair system; remove students from targets; STEM post-study visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL; 50k Syrian refugees; reopen Dubs (3k children); 28-day detention limit; allow work after 6 months; protect LGBT+ asylum seekers.

International/defence
- Support UN/NATO; spend 0.7% aid, 2% defence; suspend Saudi arms sales; tighter export controls.
- Cybersecurity investment; three-boat, reduced-readiness nuclear deterrent; lead on disarmament.

Political reform and devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Commons/local; elected Lords; cap donations; tougher lobbying; televised debates.
- Constitutional convention for a federal UK; devolution on demand in England; deliver promises to Scotland, more powers to Wales; protect NI settlement and single market interests.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Conservative', 'Labour', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Scottish National Party', 'UK Independence Party']
}
